exposure: combined strategy of postpartum haemorrhage management (TEG assessment, early surgical haemostasis, mechanical uterine compression, intrauterine balloon tamponade)
cohort: The study included 119 women experiencing obstetric haemorrhage.
finding: The proposed combined strategy for obstetric haemorrhage management significantly reduced the number of peripartum hysterectomies and total blood loss compared to standard management.
mod_finding: The combined strategy for obstetric haemorrhage management was evaluated specifically during caesarean section.
